decision_rule: PASS iff 0 NaN/Inf steps AND mean(loss_total) over the second half of the final 20% of steps <= mean(loss_total) over the first half of that same window (a still-converging-at-the-tail check, not just first-epoch-vs-last-epoch)
interpretation: Smoke run against REAL data (48 cases, 16 per dataset from kits/pancreas/liver's frozen train-split manifest, real 128^3 preprocessed volumes) at the real target scale (grid_shape=8x8x8, 512 tokens), on HF Jobs t4-medium GPU. All four pretraining objectives (L_recon, L_masked, L_struct, L_topology) wired per formalization Section 7, plus the ZBroadcast fix ensuring GraphHead and FusionHead (which Section 7's four objectives, read literally, never touch) also receive real gradient via the reconstruction path. 0 NaN/Inf steps across all 72. Loss fell substantially and monotonically by epoch (27.0 -> 19.4 -> 10.1 -> 2.1 across epoch boundaries), and kept decreasing within the smoke run's own final-20% window (4.48 -> 2.77), satisfying the decision rule with margin, not just barely. Gradient norm rose through the fitting phase (18 -> 51 peak around step 45) then fell as loss dropped (51 -> 24 by the final step) -- the shape expected of a model actually fitting rather than oscillating; gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0) was active throughout as a stability safeguard but never needed to mask instability (no NaN/Inf occurred). Two real fixes were required to get here, not just wiring: (1) gate_2.json's flagged bucket-read latency (~100-150s/case) was eliminated by materializing the case subset to local disk once via a parallel ThreadPoolExecutor copy, plus caching each case's real ph_vector once via a ProcessPoolExecutor instead of recomputing gudhi every epoch (data/local_cache.py); (2) a latent bug in compute_persistence_summary, present since Phase 0b and never caught by Gate 0/2 (which only checked finiteness, never magnitude), returned unbounded raw persistence statistics (observed up to ~19,561 on synthetic data) -- this drove L_topology's loss to ~65M in an initial local dry run before being fixed with a log1p transform at the source. This is exactly the class of finding Gate 3's smoke-before-full-run discipline exists to catch cheaply.

full_run.interpretation: Full run over all 533 real train-split cases (kits+pancreas+liver), 50 epochs, 13300 steps, ~97 minutes of training on t4-medium. 0 NaN/Inf steps across the entire run. Loss fell from a first-20%-of-steps mean of 0.732 to a final-20% mean of 0.213 -- a >3x reduction -- and was still decreasing within that final window (0.215 -> 0.212), not plateaued-then-diverging. Gradient norm settled to a small, stable range (mean 3.08, well below the 1.0 clip threshold's multiples seen early in the smoke run), consistent with a model that has genuinely converged rather than one still being held stable only by clipping. Interrupted once at epoch 23/step 6165 by a transient local network drop in the log-streaming client (httpx.ConnectError, DNS resolution failure) -- confirmed via `hf jobs inspect` that the remote job itself was unaffected (still RUNNING), re-attached via `hf jobs logs -f` with no data lost, since the job runs independently of the local log stream and checkpoints every epoch regardless.
